dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: I read that people spend four hours a day on social media. Do you find that worrying?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Honestly, yes. I think it has a huge influence on how we see ourselves.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: In what way? Many people say it simply helps them stay connected.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It does, but comparing your life with perfect images online can damage self-esteem.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: That is true. And what about the information we read there?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That is my main concern. Misleading news spreads much faster than facts.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: Do you think the platforms should be responsible for that?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Partly. I believe governments should regulate them more strictly, as long as freedom of speech is protected.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: Regulation is tricky. Who decides what is true?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Fair point. Maybe the solution is education: teaching people to check their sources.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: I agree. What about privacy? Companies collect so much data about us.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That worries me too. Most users never read the terms and conditions before accepting them.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: Some people even admit they are addicted to their phones.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I would not go that far, but I do notice that I check mine automatically.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.text: So would you ever quit social media entirely?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Probably not, but I am trying to limit my time, and it already makes a difference.
